title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages: V is a real Euclidean plane carrying a regular polygon with symmetry group D, a dihedral group of order 2m, where m = 2n (n=3 gives the hexagon, |D|=12). D^+ ≅ μ_m is the rotation subgroup and a_0 is rotation by π. V^{**} is a complexified complement, presumably of the dihedral line arrangement, with PΣ^* ≅ V^{**} up to C^*. Grothendieck wants presentations of the fundamental groupoids Π_1 PΣ^*, Π_1 V^{**} and Π_1 Σ^*, using base points stable under the full symmetry group.

Step 1 (diagonalisation, ref. (18)). V_C = V⊗C splits as the sum of its two isotropic lines V_C^ω, for ω in the two-element set ω̲ = {ω, ω'}; these are the 'circular points'. The torus-type group μ_m^{ω̲}, of order m^2, acts coordinatewise as in (32): (λ_ω)·(x_ω) = (λ_ω x_ω).

Step 2 (factorisation, (33)). Both μ_m (homotheties) and D^+ act through this group:
- μ_m embeds diagonally;
- D^+ ≅ μ_m(ω) maps by λ ↦ (λ^{A(ω)})_ω, with A(ω) = ±1, since a rotation acts by λ on one isotropic line and by λ^{-1} on the other.

Step 3 (the combined map, (34)). The map D^+ × μ_m → μ_m^{ω̲} is (λ, μ) ↦ (λμ, λ^{-1}μ), between groups of the same order m^2 = 4n^2.
- Kernel: λμ = λ^{-1}μ = 1 forces λ = μ = ±1. So the kernel has order 2, generated by (a_0, -1).
- Image: index 2, consisting of pairs (x, y) with xy = μ^2 a square in μ_{2n}. Equivalently (35): (x y)^n = 1. This is also equivalent to (x/y)^n = 1, because y^{2n} = 1.

Step 4 (begun here, finished on p.54). The automorphisms of V_C that stabilise V^{**}, i.e. induce an automorphism of Σ preserving the configuration, are exactly those coming from D × C^*. Those preserving each isotropic line come from D^+ × C^*. Consequently, elements of μ_{2n}^{ω̲} violating (35) do not stabilise V^{**}.

Purpose: determine the exact finite symmetry group (D × μ_{2n})/{±1} × {1,τ}, where τ is presumably complex conjugation. Base points (tangential or otherwise) for the Teichmüller-type groupoids are then to be chosen stable under it. This is the preparatory symmetry bookkeeping for a 'symmetric base points' presentation, in the spirit of the Esquisse's genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid program.
errors: No mathematical errors. The kernel, index and image description (35) are correct, and the equivalence with (37) on the next page holds because λ^{2n}=1.
The notation 'D^+ ×_{μ_m(ω̲)} μ_m' in (34) is just the direct product D^+ × μ_m (with D^+ identified with μ_m(ω)). It is not a fibre product, so the subscript is misleading.

ideas.what: Use the eigenline decomposition of the complexified plane into its two isotropic lines to linearise the joint action of rotations and scalar roots of unity on the dihedral configuration.
ideas.modern_name: simultaneous diagonalisation / maximal torus action on a complexified reflection representation

ideas.what: Compute the kernel (generated by (a_0,-1)) and the index-2 image {(∏λ_ω)^n = 1} of D^+ × μ_{2n} → μ_{2n}^2.
Identify the automorphisms of V_C stabilising the arrangement complement as those coming from D × C^*, in preparation for choosing symmetry-stable base points for fundamental groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: symmetry-invariant (tangential) base points for fundamental groupoids of moduli/arrangement complements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme); later Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the general philosophy of base points stable under symmetries for Teichmüller groupoids, not this specific computation

deep.surprise_reason: This page is routine bookkeeping: the symmetry group of a complexified dihedral (regular-polygon) arrangement, analysed via its isotropic lines, with an elementary kernel/image computation. It serves the known program of presenting Teichmüller groupoids with symmetric base points and contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Header '(1[-5-]) (18)' is a back-reference to formula (18): '(1̶5̶) (18)'.
In (33) the exponent reads λ^{A(ω)} (A(ω)=±1), not λ^{Aω} as a product.
The phrase before (34) reads roughly 'tel que les actions de μ_m, D^+ sur V^{**} se factorisent via celles de μ_m^{ω̲}'.
'[-dit-] groupes de = ordre' should be 'entre groupes de même ordre m^2 = 4n^2'.
The last line likely reads 'qui stabilise [the configuration], sont ceux qui proviennent-' continuing as 'ment de D mod C^*' on p.54.
